turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Can you tell me what brought you in here today?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Sure, I've been feeling very short of breath for the past, uh, two weeks, but even before that, I started feeling a little bit short of breath and I can't stop coughing and it just feels like it's really hard for me to breathe.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, so this started two weeks ago?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, it started two weeks ago.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and you're also coughing?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and how long have you been coughing for?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: The same amount of time, it started about, maybe three weeks ago, I started coughing more, um, but now it's worse.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and what kind of cough are you having? Is it a wet cough or a dry cough?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It's definitely wet. My phlegm looks green.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and how long have you noticed it being green?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It's been like that for the past two weeks.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and before that, were you having coughing as well?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, before that I was still coughing but not as much.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, uhm, and was there anything that happened, uh, did you get sick at all recently, or were you in contact with anyone who was sick?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, not that I know of.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any kind of fevers at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no fevers.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Have you noticed any kind of, uh, coughing up blood or blood tinged sputum at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm no not that, no blood.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and how much sputum are you bringing up in an average day now?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, I'm bringing up about, I'd say it would fill like two, two of my palms, like the inside of my palm.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Alright, and is your coughing like constant or does it come and go?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It's pretty constant now.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And have you had at all any kind of, uh, fevers or anything like that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No fevers.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and how about your shortness of breath? Is that, when does that happen? Is it mainly with exercise and exertion, or can it happen even when you're just going on about your day?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, its, uh, ok, its more with exertion, but right now even at rest, I'm coughing and feeling short of breath.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And are you feeling at all any kind of, uh, chest tightness or pain?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, yeah, some chest tightness.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And is that mainly when you're coughing and short of breath or, uhm, at other times as well?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, other times as well.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Are you having any other, any other like, can you describe your chest pain a little bit? Is it kind of a pressure pain or is it a sharp pain, aching pain? How would you describe it?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, I would say it's a, uh, it's a tightness in my chest. And it feels, I guess throbbing or achy?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and does this pain, uhm, move to anywhere else or does it just stay in your chest?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, it just stays in my chest.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, have you been feeling dizzy or have you fainted at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Have you been feeling increased sweating and confusion? Anything like that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, have you felt your heart racing and anything like that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Alright, and is there anything that makes your symptoms better or worse?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, I guess activity makes it worse, un, and like cold air, things like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And other than that, have you recently at all traveled outside of the country or outside of the province?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no. No, not recently.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, now are you having any wheezing at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, some wheezing, yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And any kind of headaches or nausea or vomiting.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, nothing like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and any fevers or chills.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Ah, nope, nothing like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Any night sweats?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Ah, sometimes I feel sweaty, but that's just with the shortness of breath.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and how long does your shortness of breath usually last?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It lasts about, uh, I don't know, I kind of feel short of breath all the time, but when it's really bad, it lasts about five-ten minutes and then it goes back to like my normal shortness of breath.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And has this happened to you before?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm no, I don't think so.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Like not, not this bad, I've always had some shortness of breath but nothing like this.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And , uh, do you have any kind of diarrhea or constipation?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, no nothing like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, how about fatigue?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I feel fatigued.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and is that just about today or is it, do you think it's because of your shortness of breath?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, it's probably cause of my shortness of breath.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Are you having any of these symptoms when you're trying to sleep?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: uh yeah, I think its, yeah when I'm laying down sometimes I feel more short of breath than usual, but once I shift positions it goes back to it's normal.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Ok. Is it, do you ever have to wake up at night to catch a breath or anything like that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Ah, no, it doesn't wake me up.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And have you noticed any kind of, uh, significant weight loss or anything like that recently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and have you at all had any changes in your appetite or anything like that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no change in appetite.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Any exposures to any like dust, fumes or any irritants recently

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK And, in the past, have you been diagnosed with any medical conditions?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm,  just COPD, uhm, and, I also have some congestive heart failure.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and when were you diagnosed with both of them?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: COPD I've been, I got diagnosed about seven years ago, CHF about two years ago.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and uh, right now do you have any symptoms of any swelling in your extremities like legs, hands or anything like that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Some swelling in, some swelling in my legs, yeah?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and do you have any kind of shortness of breath when you're lying down, at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, a little bit. Yeah, a little bit I would say.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And any other medical conditions?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Nope, no others.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Any allergies?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Any medications you're on right now?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah I'm on, uh, an ACE inhibitor, I'm on, uh, Spironolactone, uhm, I'm on, I have some puffers for my COPD. I believe, what do I have, I have, um, I have a long acting beta agonist. And I guess I have a short acting as well for when I need it.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And do you have, so is it just the two, two puffers?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Mhm.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and are you using, like the blue one, the blue one more at all, are you having to use the short acting one more?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I'm definitely using the short acting more, like I'm using it almost every day.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And does it help at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh I4 think so.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK yeah, so other than that, are you on any other medications?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: No, OK. And have you been taking your Spironolactone?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I've been taking all my medications.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any previous hospitalizations or surgeries?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I was hospitalised two years ago for shortness of breath and some low oxygen, that's when they diagnosed me with CHF.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: I see OK and did they say at all, It was caused by, like your COPD or what was it caused by? Do you remember?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm,  I guess just, yeah, I'm not really too sure, they said I had some heart condition and my heart isn't functioning as well as it should be. They did an echo on me.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and have you at all had any kind of heart attacks or anything like that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: No, OK. and did they, when you were having shortness of breath, did you have a like a pneumonia or infection that you had to get antibiotics for any or anything like that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, no. Actually I might have gotten some antibiotics at one point, but not during that visit.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. OK, And currently right now do you smoke?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I stopped smoking two years ago.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah no, that's really good. And definitely with these symptoms and your condition that definitely helps to quit smoking whenever you can, so congratulations for that. Any alcohol at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I drink some alcohol. I drink maybe once a week.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and any recreational drugs like marijuana?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I smoke once in a while.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, how often would you say you smoke marijuana?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I smoke about a joint a week.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and uh, do you use a, like the provincial marijuana, or do you have any other source, what would you say you use?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I use uhm, Pardon me, what was that? Do I use?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Like uh, do you get it from a store that sells the joint?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I get it from like a medical dispensary.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, OK, I see. Yeah, I just want to make sure because some, if you get it from other sources there might be more irritants in there that can cause some of your symptoms and for them to get worse as well. So yeah.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Oh I see, I see, OK.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah, and other than that, do you have any questions or concerns at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, what do you think I should do from, For now?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah, so right now what we're going to do is because you're having the coughing, shortness of breath, and you have a history of COPD & CHF, we definitely want to make sure that you're not having, uhm, what I think you might be having isn't just an exacerbation of your COPD, and especially with the green sputum it might be like a bacterial infection that's causing your symptoms to get worse, so we'll do all the appropriate testing, we'll do, a chest X-ray, we'll get some blood work done as well, w'ell give you some uh, Ventolin as well while you're here, and we might give you like a steroid medication as well. So we'll do some of those things right now for you to kind of help you right now, as well as do some of those tests that I mentioned. Depending on what comes back, you might require an admission to the hospital just because we want to make sure you don't go home with an exacerbation, especially with the CHF as well, we need to, we will need to get that under control because that can get worse with your COPD exacerbation as well. So we need to make sure some of that, swelling goes down, if we need to adjust your medications while you're here. So yeah, let's just, I'll get back to you, we'll do some of those testing and then see where to go from there. Is that OK?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, that sounds great. Thank you.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: You're welcome.
